Area.evidence_source: A total of 17 men had made no attempts on their lives and yet reported equally problematic childhoods and as many social problems as those who had made suicide attempts. Many 'tough old lags' presented themselves as having high levels of mastery over their future: While their lives usually fell short of their ideals, namely enough money, a family home and a job, they generally had clear plans for the future, were determinedly self-reliant and, despite ongoing problems, perceived themselves to be emotionally well most of the time, maintaining that they had never considered suicide as an option and distancing themselves from those who had:
